title: The Two Closest Keys

concept.title: The closest pair is always neighbours in sorted order
body: What is the smallest difference between two values of the tree? Comparing every pair would take O(n^2). But the two values with the smallest difference must be **neighbours in sorted order**: if some value lay between them, it would make a smaller difference with one of them. And the in-order walk of a BST gives the values in sorted order, so it is enough to compare each value with the **previous** value of the walk.

body.code:
def min_diff(root):
    best = None
    prev = None
    stack, cur = [], root
    while stack or cur is not None:
        while cur is not None:
            stack.append(cur)
            cur = cur.left
        cur = stack.pop()
        if prev is not None and (best is None or cur.val - prev < best):
            best = cur.val - prev
        prev = cur.val
        cur = cur.right
    return best

body: Remembering the previously visited value while walking is a typical technique for sorted structures. The differences are always non-negative because the walk is increasing. The tree has at least two nodes, so the answer always exists.

statement: Given a binary search tree with at least two nodes, print the smallest difference between the values of two different nodes.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.
The tree is a binary search tree (all values are different).

examples.note: The sorted values are 1 2 3 4 6; the smallest gap is 1.

hints: In sorted order, the closest two values are neighbours.
Walk the tree in-order and remember the previous value.
Update the best difference with the difference to the previous value.

input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root
